newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kabel 1 applies to expand programming. [CORRECTED 11:36 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Kabel 1 applies to expand programming. [CORRECTED 11:36 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline and text to make clear Kabel 1 has not yet received permission to expand its programming. Replaces story originally transmitted March 13).
Private German television network Kabel 1 said it had applied for permission to widen the scope of its licence, which would allow it to expand into news and documentary programming.
Kabel 1, which made the statement on Thursday, is owned by Pro Sieben Media AG. It needs the green light from the Bavarian State Centre for New Media (BLM).
The expansion of programming would include documentaries and news shows as well as comedies and dramas in the first half of this year.
"We expect this expansion of our programming to give us, along with an extraordinary chance for growth, an even more secure media-political position," said Kabel 1 head Ludwig Bauer.
The Pro Sieben group, which in 1996 posted its best returns, plans to go public on the Frankfurt stock exchange later this year.
